messages:
IncidentBot: paging @oncall_sre_alex: service:redwood-api (us-east-1) elevated 5xx rate detected 02:11 UTC, rolling spike impacting ~18% of requests. Severity: high. Links: https://monitoring.redwood/status/alerts/6512

oncall_sre_alex: I'm awake, looking. I can see error rate jump and elevated p50/p95 latencies. Reproducing with a few curl checks.

oncall_sre_alex: /srv/logs shows timeout to model-router pool, several 504s, and a surge of concurrent requests to model-variant:opt-4bit-llama2

ic_maya: taking incident command. Alex + Jon please post findings here. I'll coordinate comms and on-call handoffs.

eng_lead_jon: digging into router config now. Recent rollout? No recent deploys in last 6 hours. Suspecting upstream GPU node flapping due to kernel driver OOMs. Querying node events.

oncall_sre_alex: confirmed - 3 nodes restarted by kube due to OOMKill between 02:04-02:09 UTC. Autoscaler didn't replenish fast enough; queue backlog created and proxy returned 504s.

ic_maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale up dedicated pool by +3 nodes 2) route traffic to fallback model-variant (opt-4bit-llama2-stable) 3) increase request queue timeout to 45s temporarily. Alex / Jon please execute.

eng_lead_jon: scaling and routing changes applied at 02:18 UTC. Observability shows error rate falling by 02:23 UTC.

oncall_sre_alex: queue timeout bump applied. Node pool scaled to target. Error rates dropped to baseline by 02:25 UTC.

ic_maya: good. now quick customer impact assessment for SLA/billing. We need a definitive list of impacted accounts and downtime windows. Alex, can you gather request logs + customer traffic during 02:00-02:40 UTC and flag 504/5xx errors and latencies?

oncall_sre_alex: extracting logs now. Will post counts per tenant in 10m.

ops_tess: re: status page — prep proposed message so legal/billing/CS can review before publish. Draft below. Please comment.

ops_tess: ```STATUS PAGE DRAFT (to be posted once validated):
Investigating: We are currently investigating increased error rates for the Redwood API in us-east-1. Some requests may receive 5xx responses or higher latency. Our engineers are working on mitigation. We will provide updates within 30 minutes.
Update: Mitigations applied at ~02:18 UTC; error rates returned to baseline by ~02:25 UTC. Impact window: ~02:11–02:25 UTC. If you experienced failed requests during this period, retrying requests is recommended. We will follow up with additional details and any applicable service credits.```

cs_kate: thanks Tess. I'll prepare a customer-facing email template for accounts that had measurable impact. Will wait for exact impacted tenant list + downtime windows.

billing_liam: pinging here re: SLA credit eligibility and calculation. Need exact minutes of downtime and volumes per tenant. Reminder of policy: partial outage thresholds: 30–59min -> 10% monthly credit; 60–119min -> 25%; 120+ -> 50%. For sub-30min incidents we evaluate on a case-by-case for material customer impact.

legal_zoe: we'll review all outbound customer language for statements about compensation. Avoid admitting broad liability; offer credits per SLA matrix and point to terms. Keep it factual.

oncall_sre_alex: posting initial per-tenant summary (aggregated):
- tenant: AcmeCorp: 504 counts: 124; window with >1% error rate: 02:12–02:45 UTC (33 minutes)
- tenant: NovaApps: 504 counts: 12; spike window: 02:11–02:19 UTC (8 minutes)
- tenant: EduFlow: 504 counts: 0; elevated latency only 02:14–02:20 UTC
- tenant: internal-infra: 504 counts: 3; minimal

eng_lead_jon: note: system-level routing caused queuing; some requests experienced retries server-side so actual failed operations may be lower than raw 504 counts. Use unique user request ids for final determination.

cs_kate: based on that AcmeCorp has 33 minutes of elevated failure window. Billing policy threshold is 30min -> qualifies for 10% credit. NovaApps at 8 minutes -> below threshold, suggest goodwill credit only if they escalate.

billing_liam: agree. I'll open billing task BILL-4123 to process AcmeCorp credit once CS confirms usage for the billing period. For NovaApps we can offer a one-time $200 goodwill credit or equivalent if CS wants.

cs_kate: drafting AcmeCorp message below for review. Please comment and edit.

cs_kate: ```ACMECORP DRAFT EMAIL
Hi <Name>,

We’re reaching out regarding an incident on March 6 that impacted the Redwood API in us-east-1. Between ~02:11–02:25 UTC our service experienced elevated 5xx errors affecting a subset of requests. Our engineers have implemented mitigations and the service returned to baseline.

We’ve assessed the impact to your account and found ~33 minutes of elevated failed requests during the incident window. Per our Service Level Agreement, your account qualifies for a 10% service credit for the current billing period. We will process this credit and confirm once posted to your billing portal.

If you’d like, we can schedule a short postmortem call to review root cause and any additional mitigations.

Apologies for the disruption — we know how important uptime is and we’re taking steps to reduce recurrence.

Thanks,
Kate, Customer Success (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

billing_liam: language looks fine. Two asks before processing: 1) confirm AcmeCorp's billable usage for the month to compute absolute credit amount 2) confirm credit cap isn't exceeded by promotional credits. I'll create BILL-4123 and assign to accounting after CS attach usage numbers.

legal_zoe: tweak: remove "we know how important uptime is" — keep it terse. Also change "we will process this credit" -> "we will arrange for a 10% credit to be applied to your next invoice". Otherwise ok.

cs_kate: updated draft with legal edits. Putting final draft below; will send after billing confirms processing timeline.

cs_kate: ```FINAL ACMECORP EMAIL
Hi <Name>,

We’re reaching out regarding an incident on March 6 that impacted the Redwood API in us-east-1. Between ~02:11–02:25 UTC our service experienced elevated 5xx errors affecting a subset of requests. Our engineers implemented mitigations and the service returned to baseline.

We’ve assessed the impact to your account and found approximately 33 minutes of elevated failed requests during the incident window. Per our Service Level Agreement, your account qualifies for a 10% service credit for the current billing period. We will arrange for a 10% credit to be applied to your next invoice and will confirm once posted to your billing portal.

If you’d like, we can schedule a short postmortem call to review root cause and any additional mitigations.

Regards,
Kate, Customer Success (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

billing_liam: created BILL-4123 and linked incident 6512. Assigned to accounting with due-date EOD tomorrow to post credit. Ticket: https://billing.redwood/tickets/BILL-4123

eng_lead_jon: technical followups: 1) add node memory guardrails and OOM eviction alert 2) tighten autoscaler target to replace nodes faster during memory pressure 3) add fallback routing policy to reduce blast radius when pool degrades. I'll create infra tasks and assign.

oncall_sre_alex: confirming we've exported request ids + trace ids for AcmeCorp to CS for reconciliation. Also archiving logs to incident bundle.

ic_maya: thanks team. Next steps: - CS to send final email once billing confirms - Ops to post status page update (final) summarizing impact and mitigation - Eng to file infra followups and link to postmortem - Billing to post credit and close BILL-4123 - Legal to keep the customer language record. I'll close this thread once email sends and billing confirms.

ops_tess: posting final status page update now with agreed wording. Link: https://status.redwood/incident/6512-summary

cs_kate: email sent to AcmeCorp at 04:12 UTC. Billing updated BILL-4123: credit scheduled, will reflect on next invoice. Closing loop with customer if they reply.

nic_maya: incident moved to resolved at 04:20 UTC. Postmortem draft assigned to eng_postmortems JIRA-988. Thanks everyone.

IncidentBot: Incident 6512 -> resolved. Summary: root cause: node OOM leading to node restarts and insufficient autoscaler replacement; mitigation: scale + routing fallback + timeout bump; customer credit: AcmeCorp 10% per SLA; followups: infra guardrails, autoscaler tuning.
